_meta.indication: XEPI is a quinolone antimicrobial indicated for the topical treatment of impetigo due to Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes in adult and pediatric patients 2 months of age and older.

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active- (retapamulin) controlled trial in pediatric (≥2 years) and adult patients with bullous or non-bullous impetigo; randomized 1:1:1 to ozenoxacin, placebo, or retapamulin, twice daily for 5 days.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and pediatric patients (≥2 years) with bullous or non-bullous impetigo.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: clinical response (clinical success) in the ITTC population at the end-of-therapy visit (Visit 3, Day 6-7).
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical success at Visit 3: ozenoxacin 54/155 (34.8%) vs placebo 30/156 (19.2%); treatment difference 15.6% (95% CI: 5.8%, 25.3%), p=0.002.

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; patients randomized 1:1 to ozenoxacin 1% cream or matching placebo, twice daily for 5 days.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and pediatric patients two months of age and older with impetigo.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: clinical response (clinical success) in the ITTC population at the end-of-therapy visit (Visit 3, Day 6-7).
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical success at Visit 3: ozenoxacin 112/206 (54.4%) vs placebo 78/206 (37.9%); treatment difference 16.5% (95% CI: 6.9%, 25.8%), p<0.001.

key_safety: Very well tolerated. In pooled phase 3 trials adverse events occurred in 16/352 (4.4%) of ozenoxacin patients vs 17/361 (4.7%) placebo; the only AEs reported in ≥2 ozenoxacin patients were nasopharyngitis (4) and diarrhea (2). In the label, adverse reactions (rosacea and seborrheic dermatitis) were reported in 1 adult patient treated with XEPI. No deaths and no study-drug-related SAEs occurred in the development program.
target_moa: Ozenoxacin is a quinolone antimicrobial; its mechanism of action involves inhibition of the bacterial DNA replication enzymes DNA gyrase A and topoisomerase IV, and it is bactericidal against S. aureus and S. pyogenes.

advisory_committee.vote: This NDA was not discussed at an advisory committee meeting as there were no specific questions/issues that needed input from the committee.

summary.text: Standard NDA (505(b)) for ozenoxacin cream 1% (Xepi), a non-fluorinated quinolone, submitted June 23, 2016 for topical treatment of impetigo. The first cycle ended in a Complete Response letter due to outstanding CMC issues at the drug substance manufacturing facility; the applicant resubmitted July 17, 2017 and the NDA was approved. No accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, or priority-review designations applied.
